question: Why does the Transformer scale dot-product attention by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$, and what are the exact dimensions $h$, $d_{\text{model}}$, $d_k$, $d_v$, and $d_{ff}$ in the base model?
expected: For large $d_k$, dot products grow large in magnitude (if components of $q$ and $k$ are independent random variables with mean $0$ and variance $1$, their dot product has mean $0$ and variance $d_k$), pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients; scaling by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ counteracts this (Attention Is All You Need, Sec. 3.2.1, Footnote 1). The base model uses $h=8$ heads, $d_{\text{model}}=512$, $d_k=d_v=d_{\text{model}}/h=64$, and inner feed-forward dimension $d_{ff}=2048$ across $N=6$ encoder and decoder layers (Sec. 3.1, 3.2.2, 3.3, Table 3).
